answer: After the planks are fitted, the caulker drives oakum into every seam and signs the seam book beside the hull it sealed. A dawn seam claimed as caulked fails the book: the oakum must sit tight at the raven of the seam, and a seam never caulked weeps water at once. Faking a season of caulking means hiring a caulker, forging ninety signings and paying 8,900, while the trellis book is read before every launching, so a hull whose seams were never caulked stays ashore.
